actionable_steps.citation: Asuuya and dhwesha : the deadly vices — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 17 (1984), 1984-09-06
actionable_steps.step: The next time someone does well, practise feeling genuinely happy for them — learn to enjoy another's prosperity and happiness until it becomes your reflex.

actionable_steps.citation: Asuuya and dhwesha : the deadly vices — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 17 (1984), 1984-09-06
actionable_steps.step: Uproot jealousy the way Swami prescribes: cultivate love and dedicate all your actions to God. Reading about it is not enough — constant effort is required.

actionable_steps.citation: Kith and kin of all — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 6 (1966), 1966-10-25
actionable_steps.step: Practise devotion with humility — bhakti makes you humble and kills envy. See the other person as your own image, not your rival.

actionable_steps.citation: Overcome Jealousy With Love — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 33 (2000), 2000-12-25
actionable_steps.step: Watch for jealousy's three children — desire, anger and hatred — and catch them at birth, before they grow.

actionable_steps.citation: Reduce Your Desires — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 35 (2002), 2002-05-24
actionable_steps.step: Do a daily honesty check: did I resent anyone's happiness today? If yes, replace it with one good wish for them.

definition.citation: Ramayana - The Essence Of The Vedas — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 34 (2001), 2001-04-02
definition.quote: Jealousy is the worst of all evil qualities. Three-fourths of the world is ruined because of jealousy.

discourses.citation: Jealousy the root cause of evil — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 26 (1993), 1993-07-03
discourses.quote: It is the hand of Asuuya (jealousy). This is a dire malady which has entered all spheres of life in the world today. There is a remedy even for the dreaded disease of cancer. But there is no way of curing the malaise of jealousy.

discourses.citation: Asuuya and dhwesha : the deadly vices — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 17 (1984), 1984-09-06
discourses.quote: The man filled with jealousy and hatred is like a blind man who cannot see the sun however brightly he may shine. He cannot see God however near God may be.

discourses.citation: Asuuya and dhwesha : the deadly vices — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 17 (1984), 1984-09-06
discourses.quote: Because of its egregious evil tendency, jealousy should be rooted out from the very beginning. You must learn to enjoy at another's prosperity and happiness.

discourses.citation: Kith and kin of all — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 6 (1966), 1966-10-25
discourses.quote: Bhakthi or the attitude of devotion and dedication makes you humble and kills envy; jnana or the awareness of your being an integral part of God, who is all this, makes you kin with all, and there is no place for distinction, which breeds envy.

make_it_real: Swami's test is simple: be as happy at another's joy as if it had happened to you. Try it once today — and watch the envy starve.
title: Jealousy & Envy

vahinis.quote: The root cause of all anxieties and calamities of man is envy. … Envy is invariably accompanied by hatred. These two are twin villains. They are poisonous pests. They attack the very roots of one's personality.
